correctness.rationale: Complete proof: every subsequence embedding in paired arches must use the two letters of an indexed arch; this yields a forbidden transition matrix product. The Thue–Morse complement identity and Cayley–Hamilton give d_{j+1}=s_j^2+2 and s_{j+1}=s_j d_j from det(P_j)=1, with initial (d_0,s_0)=(2,1); the resulting nonlinear scalar formula is exact. A rescaled logarithmic recurrence is contractive and its correction terms summable, proving the displayed limiting base. Independent direct greedy-subsequence counts, exact matrix products, and direct enumerations were executed for bounded parameter ranges; these do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The canonical automatic Thue–Morse family and dyadic prefixes are natural, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Every-level exact absent-subsequence counts and their distinct non-Fibonacci nonlinear evolution reveal a new substitution invariant. The sharp limiting exponential base quantifies sparsity among missing candidates and explains a structural difference from maximal Fibonacci arch concatenations. The result has a full infinite proof rather than a small numerical increment.
